title: Kula Community Meeting: Fire Preparedness July 23, 2024

issues.title: Evacuation software and new evacuation zones
Power shutoffs during high wind and low humidity
State fire code adoption with brush clearing fines
Possible county purchase of Maui Land and Pine water assets

recap.headline: Kula meeting reviews Crater Road fire response, evacuation alerts and Upcountry water
recap.in_60_seconds: Councilmember Yuki Lei Sugimura hosted a Kula community meeting on fire preparedness after the Crater Road fire, with the Fire Chief, Maui Police, the Maui Emergency Management Agency (MEMA) administrator and the Water Supply director. MEMA said new evacuation software with zone maps and push alerts should be online within about a month, and urged people to sign up for MEMA Alerts, which has about 21,000 subscribers. The Fire Chief said evidence points to an accidental electrical ignition for the Crater Road fire, and that fire code changes would expand fuel clearing from 30 feet up to 100 feet. The Water director said 7 more large generators are being bought and 4 new Upcountry wells studied, but 51 water sites would still lack generators. About two dozen audience questions were answered, mostly from written slips. Still open are a second evacuation route for lower Pukalani, a statewide firefighting aircraft program, and when MEMA will fill 13 open positions.

parts.title: Welcome and purpose of the meeting
parts.presenter: Council staff and Councilmember Yuki Lei Sugimura
presented: Panel included Maui Police, the Fire Chief, the MEMA administrator and the Water Supply director.
Meeting was called after the Crater Road fire left Upcountry residents anxious.
Questions could be written on slips and collected for the panel.

parts.title: Evacuation planning and the fire department's role
presented: Evacuation routes depend on incident type, location and expected impact; there is no single fixed route.
Fire responds to about 250 to 300 wildfires a year in Maui County and has historically evacuated only a handful of times.
Over-evacuating can cause gridlock, so evacuations are sequenced.
Any agency, including police, can start an evacuation.

parts.title: Police role in evacuations
presented: Officers go door to door but cannot force people to leave.
Officers drive private or unfamiliar routes first before sending residents on them.
Police will cut locks or push down fences if needed to get people out.

parts.title: Alerts, County Communications and new evacuation technology
presented: MEMA Alerts grew from about 19,000 to nearly 21,000 subscribers after a recent expo.
Alerts also go out by TV/radio emergency alerts, cell phone wireless alerts and County press releases; County social media reaches about 60,000.
New community evacuation modeling software will estimate evacuation times and road gaps.
Zone-based evacuation software will send push alerts with maps and a public web page.

raised.concern: Whether a solar or geomagnetic storm could knock out alert systems.
Organizing neighborhoods to help in emergencies.

answered.said: No single alert system works alone; TV, radio, cell and other tools are used together because some will fail.
There is a plan to organize and prepare communities, but MEMA first needs to fill positions to lead it.

parts.title: Review of the Crater Road fire response
parts.presenter: MEMA Administrator, Fire Chief and police lieutenant
presented: The emergency operations center activated July 10 and ran four straight days; 150 to 200 cars cut off above the fire were brought out 10 at a time.
Winds were 0 to 5 mph below mile marker 6.5 but gusted to 45 mph above it; eucalyptus threw embers past containment lines.
National Guard sent two military helicopters to drop water; the shelter moved to King Kekaulike High School for capacity.
Perimeter has held since July 13, but hot soil and lava tubes keep reigniting the fire.

parts.title: Water system, generators and new Upcountry water sources
parts.presenter: Director of the Department of Water Supply
presented: Water systems were built for structure fires, not wildfires; the County has 47 wells and 32 booster pumps but 12 permanent and 6 portable generators, all portables stationed Upcountry.
Three more generators were rented and 7 are being bought at about $500,000 each, taking about a year to deliver; 51 sites would still lack generators, about $25 million.
Four new Upcountry wells are being studied; private wells including Kula 1800 and a Maui Land and Pineapple well are being evaluated.
A pipeline connecting the Central and Upcountry systems is being considered; a 2003 consent decree blocks County wells in the Haʻikū area.

next.what: Hydraulic model of the water system completed

raised.concern: How water generators turn on during power outages or utility power shutoffs.
Status of the State agricultural water line above upper Kula for firefighting.
Water pressure and hydrants versus standpipes in Upcountry neighborhoods.
What caused the recent fires, and a request for timely public notice of causes.
Whether evacuation centers are ready to open immediately.
Whether the CERT volunteer program still exists and can help in evacuations.
Request for MEMA advisories every four hours while a fire is not contained.
Whether a firefighting airplane reported on Oʻahu could be used on Maui.
When outdoor sirens are sounded.
Who staffs the emergency operations center during a fire, and whether MEMA is fully staffed.
Whether Homeland Security grant money can help water infrastructure.
Where water for the Crater Road fire came from and whether supply was enough.
Cost, timing and bond funding for connecting Central and Upcountry water systems.
When local weather stations will be installed.
A dedicated emergency radio station.
Requiring vacant landowners to clear overgrowth and fire fuel.
Evacuation routes out of lower Pukalani and Upcountry besides Haleakalā and Kula highways.
Cost of pumping water Upcountry, daily and in drought.
How the County handles houseless people living in fire-prone areas.
Whether departments are seeking bond funding for generators, water and technology upgrades.

answered.said: Automatic switches are being installed so generators start on their own when power goes out.
The State-built line uses the same source as the treatment plant, so it adds no new water, but is being evaluated with the new hydraulic model.
Older neighborhoods met the code of their time with standpipes; hydrants come with new subdivisions and development because retrofits are costly.
Many wildfire causes stay undetermined, but evidence points to an accidental electrical ignition for the Crater Road fire; work continues with ATF on others.
Red Cross aims to open shelters within two hours and reached the Piʻihana fire in about 40 minutes; temporary evacuation points will give information first.
CERT is active, with a train-the-trainer course in August and plans for two to three a year.
Once the emergency center downgrades, MEMA Alerts stop and updates come through County press releases and department social media.
No such plane is known to be available; fire chiefs asked the governor for a statewide aircraft program, though fixed-wing planes have refill limits.
Sirens can be used for any threat to tell people to seek more information.
Only partners needed for the problem are in the small center; MEMA has about seven staff against 22 approved positions and plans to fill 13 more.
Yes; many water projects appear on the hazard mitigation list he ranked that day.
Most water came from Crater Road area hydrants; military helicopters refilled at a reservoir or the ocean.
It would cost $10 to $20 million, take at least two to three years, and could use revenue bonds or outside funding.
The department is working with the State and Hawaiian Electric on weather stations and public camera and weather websites.
Public information and outreach positions are approved; more use of radio will come once they are staffed.
Code now requires fuel cut to 18 inches within 30 feet of a structure; amendments would extend this up to 100 feet, plus Firewise work and yearly April checks with large landowners.
A lower Pukalani exit would need a right-of-entry agreement with the landowning association; new subdivisions need two exits and older ones should work with neighbors.
Modeling software will find route gaps to prioritize road links; some areas are safer to shelter in place.
Pumping costs about $10 per thousand gallons before overhead; the department now pumps more to keep reservoirs full.
Several departments are working at the Old Maui High School area; people cannot simply be removed and landowners must act.
About 140 water projects totaling about $1 billion are being matched to over 40 federal funding sources and State low-interest loans.
No new fire station has opened since 2003; $15.1 million for a Haʻikū fire station awaits the federal appropriations bill.

next.what: Federal appropriations bill with Haʻikū fire station money

parts.title: Closing remarks and final question
presented: Thanked staff, panelists and Akaka; noted a vacant lot near Pukalani was cleared of dry brush.
South Maui Councilmember Tom Cook, Water and Infrastructure Committee chair, said the Council is funding water source work and expects more source in coming years.

raised.concern: How many Upcountry wells and pumps have generators and how ready they are during a power shutoff.

answered.said: Upcountry is served by 5 wells and 11 pumps; the portable generators sit at key pump stations, all work, and he rated readiness 8 or 9 out of 10.

bills.name: 2003 consent decree
bills.what: A County agreement that bars new County wells in the Haʻikū area until its requirements are met.

bills.name: Fire code amendments
bills.what: Planned changes to clarify fuel clearing rules and extend clearing up to 100 feet depending on vegetation.

bills.name: Federal appropriations bill
bills.what: Would include $15.1 million for a Haʻikū fire station.

open_questions.question: Will a second evacuation route be opened from lower Pukalani across private land?
Will the State create a statewide firefighting aircraft program?
When will MEMA fill its 13 open positions, including public information staff?
When will new Upcountry weather stations be installed?

moments.quote: If there's private roads or anything that we might have to use, we'll try as best as we can to make sure our officers drive those routes first.
moments.about: Describes how police check private roads before sending evacuees on them.

moments.quote: I can click on zone 1, 2, and 3 that puts them in imminent danger and or red. Kind of notification that you guys need to move out now. There's a danger coming from this particular direction. I need you guys to evacuate.
moments.about: Explains how the new zone-based evacuation software lets MEMA put specific zones on evacuate, standby or advisory status quickly.

moments.who: Director of the Department of Water Supply
moments.quote: There's a Maui, Lāna and Pine well that's in the area. We've been talking to them about potentially getting their well connected to our system.
moments.about: Reports early county talks about connecting a Maui Land and Pine upcountry well to the county water system.

moments.who: Director of the Department of Water Supply
moments.quote: But we are implementing technologies that would allow an automatic switch over. So if the power goes off, the generator automatically comes on.
moments.about: Explains that water facilities are getting automatic generator switchovers for when the power company shuts off power.

moments.quote: The clarity of the fire code is the first thing we're working on, and we're working on our fire code amendments right now. Just to let you know what the fire code states is that 30 feet from the nearest structure, your fuel needs to be cut to 18 inches or shorter.
moments.about: Explains the current brush-clearing rule and says the department is drafting fire code amendments.

moments.quote: what we're going to do is we're going to increase that fire code to go all the way up to 100 feet depending on the size of the vegetation.
moments.about: Says the planned fire code change would extend required fuel clearing up to 100 feet depending on vegetation.

moments.quote: So, we would need to get some sort of agreement with Pukulani Association to allow a right of entry for people to evacuate on their property.
moments.about: Shows that a second evacuation route out of Lower Pukalani depends on an access agreement with a private landowner.

moments.quote: It also will identify the gap or the deficiency in evacuation routes, which would allow us to prioritize extensions of roads, connections and or additions to the road.
moments.about: Says the community evacuation modeling software will reveal weak evacuation routes and help prioritize road improvements.

moments.quote: If we were to have, let's say the PSPS program activates for upper Kula, the power is shut off. What's your comfort level of our ability to access water to fight a fire?
moments.about: Shows resident concern about whether firefighting water would be available during a utility power shutoff in Upper Kula.

moments.who: Director of the Department of Water Supply
moments.quote: Most likely it would be 8 or 9. We're in good shape.
moments.about: Gives the water director's confidence that Upcountry water would hold up for firefighting during a power shutoff.
